extracted.intended_audience: Early-career researchers (potential PIs), authorized institutional representatives, and research administrators preparing pre-applications and applications to the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science Early Career Research Program (ECRP, DE-FOA-0003602).
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting the required pre-application and full application for the Department of Energy Office of Science Early Career Research Program (ECRP), ensuring eligibility, responsiveness to program/topic areas, compliance with submission rules, and alignment with merit review expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Application Required
rubrics_metrics.description: A Pre-Application is required. Pre-Applications must be submitted by an authorized institutional representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-Applications must be submitted in PAMS (pre-application system) and submission by an authorized institutional representative confirms that the proposed research idea fits within the scope of SC-funded programs at the applicant institution, laboratory, or user facility. Applicants are encouraged to submit pre-applications well before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission by Authorized Institutional Representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a pre-application (in PAMS) or an application (in Grants.gov) by an authorized institutional representative is required and constitutes confirmation that the proposed research fits within the scope of SC-funded programs at the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This institutional submission requirement helps ensure institutional awareness/commitment and scope alignment. Deadlines and system-specific instructions (PAMS, Grants.gov) must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Applicant Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for award is restricted to U.S. Institutions of Higher Education, DOE/NNSA National Laboratories, and institutions operating SC Scientific User Facilities (per 2 CFR 910.126).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-DOE/NNSA FFRDCs and other Federal Agencies are not eligible to submit or be proposed as subrecipients. Eligibility restrictions will not be waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Sharing Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost sharing for basic and fundamental research is not required pursuant to an exclusion from Section 988 of the Energy Policy Act of 2005. Cost sharing will not be considered as a factor during merit review or award selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost sharing is not required of DOE/NNSA National Laboratories or their subcontractors at any tier. Laboratories may impose cost-sharing requirements on their contractors subject to laboratory policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Scope — Basic Research (no commercial focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: This NOFO seeks to support basic research to advance understanding rather than to address commercial opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that propose research related to current commercial activity or current customer needs may be declined without merit review.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI Career-Stage Eligibility (10-year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than 10 years can have passed between the year the PI’s Ph.D. was awarded and the calendar year in which this NOFO is released. For this competition, those who received doctorates on or after January 1, 2015, are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PI has multiple doctorates, the discipline of the one earned within the 10-year window must be relevant to the proposed research. Extensions to eligibility for major life events (three months or longer) must be validated by an institutional official and included in the pre-application.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI Employment Status by Institution Type
rubrics_metrics.description: PI employment/appointment requirements vary by applicant type: (1) Institution of Higher Education: untenured Assistant or untenured Associate Professor on the tenure track at the originating U.S. academic institution; (2) DOE/NNSA National Laboratory: full-time, permanent, non-postdoctoral national laboratory employee; (3) SC Scientific User Facility not at a DOE/NNSA National Laboratory: full-time, permanent, non-postdoctoral user facility employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PI must hold the required employment status as of the closing date for the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole and Indivisible PI Leadership — No Co-PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards under the ECRP must be under the sole and indivisible leadership of the PI. There can be no co-PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other senior or key personnel may be proposed only if their efforts are clearly and unambiguously under the direction and supervision of the PI and they commit less time and request less support than the PI. Applications including co-PIs may be declined without review. Definition: A Co-PI is an individual designated as sharing, or being delegated, a significant aspect of the PI’s authority/responsibility for the project as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI Time Commitment Expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators funded under this program are encouraged to charge at least 50% of their time to the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts less than 50% should be as close to 50% as possible. Ensuring substantial PI effort facilitates development of independent research and planning for transitions when awards end.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI Prior ECRP Awards Ineligibility / Other Early-Career Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs who have received awards previously under the SC ECRP are not eligible. PIs of early career awards funded by other agencies or entities are eligible only if the proposed research scope is different from that already funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure research scope differs from prior early-career awards to be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Right-to-Work Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: SC does not require U.S. citizenship or permanent residency for personnel, but all personnel working or proposed to work under an award must have the legal right to perform such work in the jurisdiction where the work will be performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must verify immigration/authorization status for personnel at the site(s) where work will be conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on PI Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one pre-application on behalf of a PI may be submitted in any given SC ECRP competition. A PI may not submit an application in more than three SC ECRP competitions (participation defined as submission of a full application that completed the review/decision process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawn applications prior to official decline do not count as participation; applications declined without merit review do not count. Institutions/labs may submit multiple pre-applications but must ensure ideas fit within SC scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional/Lab/Facility Scope Confirmation and Constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a pre-application or application by an authorized institutional representative is a confirmation that the proposed research idea fits within the scope of SC-funded programs at the national laboratory or user facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications from DOE National Laboratories or SC Scientific User Facilities should not (a) attempt to revive previously terminated research areas within the laboratory/facility, or (b) topically isolate investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Application Content Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-applications must clearly articulate the main scientific motivations and barriers to progress, the technical basis for overcoming those barriers, and the key insights or novel approaches for addressing the scientific and technical challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-applications that fail to articulate motivations, barriers, technical basis, or novel approaches may be considered out of scope or non-responsive for the topic area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to Specific Topic Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research under each SC program (ASCR, BES, BER, FES, HEP, NP, DOE IP) must be responsive to one of the specific topic areas listed for that program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each program lists topic-specific expectations, in-scope research areas, and explicit out-of-scope items; applicants must select and align with the appropriate topic and follow topic guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCR — Extreme-Scale Applied Mathematics: Scope & Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must address one or more grand challenges: (1) high computational and communication complexity and development of efficient algorithms; (2) better algorithm scalability for HPC; (3) reduced ill-conditioning/sensitivity for inverse problems; (4) improved algorithm reliability/robustness for future architectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-applications out of scope include research that does not address these challenges; research that does not create a body of knowledge to inform future extreme-scale science; proposals that fail to articulate motivations/barriers/technical basis/novel approaches; cryptography research; AI applications (should go to topic 2); quantum computing/networking (should go to topic 3). References to relevant workshops are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCR — Scalable Scientific AI & Automation: Scope & Out-of-Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Focuses on scientific AI for large-scale distributed (static) and real-time streaming (dynamic) data, hardware/software co-design, and autonomous/semi-autonomous robotic systems integrated with AI, HPC, and sensor fusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Out-of-scope examples include: approaches that merely apply scientific AI to a new application rather than advancing fundamental aspects of scientific AI; biomedical/agricultural/warehouse/consumer robotics unrelated to DOE missions; routine hardware refresh/commercial deployment without new scientific insight; pure teleoperation without pathway to scalable autonomy; projects whose main deliverable is a product/service rather than fundamental knowledge; cyber-physical security or facility-management projects without experiment-centric autonomy goals; quantum work belongs in topic (3).

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCR — Quantum Computing and Networking: Rigor and Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Involves innovative research integrating computer science and applied mathematics to address obstacles hindering quantum utility and application of quantum technology to DOE/ASCR mission. Research should be backed by rigorous theory and delineate a path to success with clear metrics and milestones; engagement with ASCR testbeds is encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Out-of-scope includes proposals that do not address listed topics; development of new candidate physical qubit systems or improvements to physical qubits; quantum key distribution; cryptography and cryptanalysis; projects duplicative or competitive with industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: BES — Materials Chemistry: Hypothesis-Driven 'Why' Questions Required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications MUST pose scientific questions and propose hypothesis-driven research leading to scientific understanding of chemical phenomena that play a role in synthesis, function, or degradation of energy-relevant materials. Applications will be evaluated based on their ability to formulate and address 'why' questions, prioritizing causal explanations over correlative observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be considered for this year’s ECRP, applications must propose basic research in one of three topical areas (Applied Materials Theory; Materials Chemistry Dynamics; Chemical Synthetic Methodology). Applications aimed primarily at electrochemical energy storage technologies are limited/excluded per topic guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-Specific In-Scope / Out-of-Scope Lists (general rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many program topics provide explicit in-scope research areas and enumerated out-of-scope items that define acceptable and unacceptable proposals for that topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must read topic-specific in-scope/out-of-scope lists closely and ensure their pre-application and application map to in-scope interests; failure to do so may lead to exclusion or decline without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit (Peer) Review Process Definition and Role
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit (or peer) review means the process that involves consistent application of standards and procedures that produce fair, impartial, and objective examinations of applications based on evaluation of scientific or technical merit or other relevant aspects, performed by experts in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merit review provides guidance to DOE individuals responsible for award decisions. Applications will be evaluated by reviewers against review criteria (see Review Criteria section). Non-responsive or out-of-scope applications may be excluded prior to merit review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Responsiveness Review
rubrics_metrics.description: A responsiveness review will be performed to determine whether the application meets NOFO requirements (e.g., eligibility, adherence to topic scope, required submission elements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-responsive applications (e.g., missing required institutional submission, ineligible PI, out-of-scope research, co-PI present) may be administratively excluded and not sent to merit review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget/Award Amounts and Project Period
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected total available funding and expected award amounts: e.g., $875,000 for an Institution of Higher Education, $2,750,000 for a DOE/NNSA National Laboratory or SC Scientific User Facility, with an expected project period of 5 years (subject to appropriations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recommended for funding as a lead applicant, DOE National Laboratory funding is provided through the DOE Field-Work Proposal System and work will be conducted under the laboratory’s contract with DOE; administrative provisions of the NOFO may not apply to labs in the same way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Extensions for Major Life Events
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions to the 10-year post-PhD eligibility window due to major life events (three months or longer) are possible but must be validated by a letter from a university dean, research vice president, laboratory division director, or equivalent official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The validation letter must be included in the pre-application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Responsibility for Fit and Topic Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratories and user facilities may submit multiple pre-applications but are responsible for ensuring that research ideas submitted fit within the scope of SC-funded programs at the laboratory or user facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This institutional vetting is intended to ensure applicants have the opportunity to belong to or join, at the lab/facility’s discretion, funded research groups and avoid proposals that topically isolate investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for Non-Compliance with Stated Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that do not comply with explicit NOFO requirements (e.g., ineligible applicant type or PI status, presence of co-PIs, proposing commercial-focused work, out-of-scope topic) may be declined without merit review or administratively excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should follow NOFO instructions exactly; many topic areas list explicit 'out of scope' examples that will cause exclusion.
